name: bitmagic
description: BitMagic Commander X16 Debugger and Development Solution

bitMagic.debugger.autoUpdateDebugger.description: Automatically update the local copy of the debugger.

bitMagic.officialEmulator.downloadOffici.description: Automatically download the official emulator for the ROM.BIN and symbol files.

bitMagic.officialEmulator.officialEmulat.description: Path to the official emulator that is automatically downloaded.

bitMagic.officialEmulator.customOfficial.description: Custom Location of the official emulator for the ROM.BIN and symbol files. This can be overridden in the project.json file.

bitMagic.officialEmulator.version.description: Version of the official emulator to download.

bitMagic.debugger.useBundledDotnet.description: Automatically download a copy of the dotnet runtime for the extension.

bitMagic.debugger.path.description: Path to the debugger that is automatically downloaded.

bitMagic.debugger.developRelease.description: Use the develop release channel. This is for pre-release and experimental features. Use with caution!

bitMagic.debugger.disablePlatformCheck.description: Disable the platform check, to let you experiment on non-supported platforms.

bitMagic.debugger.alternativePath.description: Path to an alternative copy of the debugger.

bitMagic.localDebug.enable.description: Use a running version of BitMagic for debugging BitMagic itself. (Will require a restart)

bitMagic.localDebug.dapPort.description: Port to use to communicate with the locally running debugger for DAP. (Only used when debugging the debugger.)

bitMagic.localDebug.lspPort.description: Port to use to communicate with the locally running debugger for LSP. (Only used when debugging the debugger.)

bitMagic.debugger.useLspProcessForDebugg.description: Run debug sessions through the same background process used for language features (IntelliSense), instead of starting a new one for every session. Faster session start. If that shared process crashes it restarts automatically; while it's unavailable, debug sessions fall back to starting their own. Experimental.

languageModelTools.name: bitmagic_getSprites
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns the current state of every VERA sprite in the active BitMagic X16 debug session. For call stack, variables, or evaluating expressions, use the standard debug tools instead - this is only for VERA sprite state. Returns JSON: { "Sprites": array of exactly 128 entries, one per hardware sprite slot (index 0-127) - most slots are unused, look at Width/Height/Address to tell which are actually active. Each entry: { "Index": slot number, "Address": VRAM address of the sprite image data, "PalletteOffset", "CollisionMask", "Width", "Height", "X", "Y", "Depth", "HFlip", "VFlip", "Mode" (4 or 8 bits-per-pixel) - all numeric/boolean and useful for analysis; "Display" is a base64-encoded PNG image of the sprite's rendered pixels - it exists for reference but isn't something you can interpret as text, use the numeric fields instead. } }

languageModelTools.name: bitmagic_getLayers
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Renders the 6 VERA compositing layers of the active BitMagic X16 debug session as images. Returns JSON: { "Display": array of exactly 6 base64-encoded PNG screenshots (640x480), one per layer, in compositing order }. This is visual/rendered output, not structured layer configuration (mode, map/tile base addresses, scroll) - there is no numeric layer state to inspect via this tool.

languageModelTools.name: bitmagic_getPalette
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns the current VERA palette (256 entries) in the active BitMagic X16 debug session. For call stack, variables, or evaluating expressions, use the standard debug tools instead - this is only for VERA palette state. Returns JSON: { "Palette": array of 256 { "R", "G", "B" } (0-255 each) - the raw VERA palette values; "DisplayPalette": array of 256 { "R", "G", "B", "A" } - the same colours converted to display-space RGBA. Index into either array with a palette index (0-255) to get a specific colour. }

languageModelTools.name: bitmagic_getCpuHistory
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns the entire recorded 65C02 instruction history (most-recent-first) in the active BitMagic X16 debug session, since the last reset or session start. Useful for understanding how execution reached the current point. For the current call stack, use the standard debug tools instead - this is raw instruction-level trace history. WARNING: this can be a very large response on a session that has been running for a while (the history buffer holds up to several hundred thousand instructions by default) - expect a large result, and consider that before calling this on a long-running session. Returns JSON: { "HistoryItems": array of { "Proc" (containing symbol name if known), "OpCode" (disassembled instruction text), "RawParameter", "RamBank", "RomBank", "Pc", "A", "X", "Y", "Sp", "Flags" (e.g. "[N V  B D I Z C]" with set flags as their letter), "SourceFile", "LineNumber", "Clock" (cycle count) }, "More": boolean (whether there are older entries beyond what's returned) }

languageModelTools.name: bitmagic_getMemoryUse
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Renders a heatmap image of which addresses have recently been executed/changed/read in the active BitMagic X16 debug session. Returns JSON: { "Display": a single base64-encoded PNG image (256x256, one pixel per address) - not structured/numeric data, this is a visual overview only. Colour meaning: red channel = executed, blue channel = read, green channel = changed (dim if only changed previously, bright if changed since the last call). } Side effect: calling this clears the tracked changed/executed/read flags it just reported, so calling it again immediately after will show a different (mostly blank) picture, not the same state repeated.

languageModelTools.name: bitmagic_readMemory
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Reads raw bytes from X16 memory/VRAM at a given address in the active BitMagic X16 debug session. For call stack, local/global variables, or evaluating expressions, use the standard debug tools instead - this is only for VERA/RAM/ROM byte-level access. Returns JSON: { "Address": the requested offset as a "0xXXXX" hex string, "UnreadableBytes": count of requested bytes past the end of the memory space (0 if the whole read was in range), "Data": the bytes as base64 (not directly readable), "bytes": the same bytes decoded as a plain number[] (0-255 each) - use this one, "bytesHex": the same bytes as a hex string, e.g. "a9002000". }

memoryReference.description: The memory space to read from: "main" for the currently-banked CPU-addressable RAM/ROM (a 64KB view - won't see RAM/ROM banks not currently switched in; use "rambank<N>"/"rombank<N>" to read a specific bank directly regardless of what's switched in); "vram" for VERA video RAM; "sdcard" for the SD card disk image (filenames, directory entries, file contents - not CPU memory, e.g. AUTOBOOT.X16 lives here, not in "main"); "sdcardblock" for the current SD card SPI transfer buffer; "nvram" for RTC NVRAM; "rambank<N>" for a specific 8KB RAM bank (e.g. "rambank3"); "rombank<N>" for a specific 16KB ROM bank (e.g. "rombank0").

offset.description: Byte offset within the memory space to start reading from.

languageModelTools.name: bitmagic_writeMemory
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Writes raw bytes to X16 memory/VRAM at a given address in the active BitMagic X16 debug session, to amend live state (e.g. poke a value to test a theory). For call stack, local/global variables, or evaluating expressions, use the standard debug tools instead - this is only for VERA/RAM/ROM byte-level access. Only "main", "vram", "sdcard" and "nvram" are writable (unlike reading/searching, "sdcardblock"/"rambank<N>"/"rombank<N>" are not supported here - a write with one of those silently writes 0 bytes rather than erroring, check the returned BytesWritten). Returns JSON: { "written": number of bytes you asked to write, "BytesWritten": number of bytes actually written by the debugger (compare to "written" - if lower or 0, the write didn't fully succeed, e.g. an unsupported memoryReference or an out-of-range offset), "Offset": the offset that was written to. }

memoryReference.description: The memory space to write to - only these four are supported for writing (unlike reading/searching): "main" for the currently-banked CPU-addressable RAM/ROM (a 64KB view - won't affect RAM/ROM banks not currently switched in); "vram" for VERA video RAM; "sdcard" for the SD card disk image; "nvram" for RTC NVRAM.

offset.description: Byte offset within the memory space to start writing at.

bytes.description: Bytes to write (each 0-255), starting at offset.

languageModelTools.name: bitmagic_searchMemory
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Searches X16 memory/VRAM for a byte pattern in the active BitMagic X16 debug session. Useful for locating where a known value (e.g. a sprite's X position, or a string like a filename) lives before reading or writing it directly. Returns JSON with exactly these fields - read Matches first, it is the only field that indicates whether anything was found: { "Matches": number[] - a list of byte offsets (relative to the start of the searched memory space) where the pattern was found; an EMPTY array [] means no matches, NOT an error or missing data. "Truncated": boolean - true only if there were more matches than maxResults and the list was cut short. "SpaceLength": number - the total size in bytes of the memory space that was searched, for context only. } Example: {"Matches":[512],"Truncated":false,"SpaceLength":65536} means exactly one match, at offset 512 (0x0200).

memoryReference.description: The memory space to search: "main" for the currently-banked CPU-addressable RAM/ROM (a 64KB view - won't see RAM/ROM banks not currently switched in; use "rambank<N>"/"rombank<N>" to search a specific bank directly regardless of what's switched in); "vram" for VERA video RAM; "sdcard" for the SD card disk image (filenames, directory entries, file contents - not CPU memory, e.g. AUTOBOOT.X16 lives here, not in "main"); "sdcardblock" for the current SD card SPI transfer buffer; "nvram" for RTC NVRAM; "rambank<N>" for a specific 8KB RAM bank (e.g. "rambank3"); "rombank<N>" for a specific 16KB ROM bank (e.g. "rombank0").

caseInsensitive.description: For byte values that represent text, match regardless of case.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of matches to return. Defaults to 500.

languageModelTools.name: bitmagic_getExceptionInfo
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Reports why the active BitMagic X16 debug session is currently stopped, when the stop was caused by an exception breakpoint (BRK/EXP/FIO) rather than a line breakpoint or a step. For the call stack or variables at the stop, use the standard debug tools instead. Returns JSON: { "exceptionId": "BRK", "EXP", "FIO" or "UNK" (no exception is why it's stopped), "description": human-readable explanation }.

languageModelTools.name: bitmagic_findMemoryValue
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Scans every RAM bank of the active BitMagic X16 debug session for a value, "Cheat Engine" style - the way to find where an unknown game variable (health, score, a counter) lives without knowing its address. Call with no locations to scan fresh: this walks all RAM banks and takes roughly 30-60 seconds regardless of which value or searchType you pick, so only call it once per hunt, not repeatedly. To narrow down, take the locations array this call returned, let the target run a bit (or change something in-game), then call again passing that same locations array back with a new searchType comparing each one's current value to what it held last time - repeat until only the address you want is left. Returns JSON: { "ToFind": the value that was searched for, "SearchType": the comparison used, "Locations": array of { "Location": an opaque id, not a plain CPU address, encodes which RAM bank a match came from - round-trip it into a follow-up call, don't use it with the memory read/write tools, "Value": the value at that location }, "Stepping": whether the target is currently single-stepping }.

toFind.description: Value to search for (searchType "Equal"/"Not Equal"/"Less Than"/"Greater Than") - ignored when searchType is "Changed"/"Not Changed"/"Gone Up"/"Gone Down", which compare against each location's previous value instead.

searchType.description: "Equal", "Not Equal", "Less Than", "Greater Than" (all compare against toFind), or - only valid on a narrowing call that passes locations back - "Changed", "Not Changed", "Gone Up", "Gone Down" (compare against each location's previous value).

locations.description: Omit for a fresh scan. On a narrowing call, pass back exactly the locations array the previous call returned.

languageModelTools.name: bitmagic_sendKey
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Sends a single keyboard event to the active BitMagic X16 debug session, exactly as a real key press/release would arrive - one event per call, not a batch. To type a character, send it down then up (call twice); hold a modifier across other keys by sending it down, sending the other keys, then sending it up. Returns JSON: { "Success": boolean, "Error": string or null }.

down.description: true for key down (press), false for key up (release).

languageModelTools.name: bitmagic_sendMouse
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Sends a single mouse sample to the active BitMagic X16 debug session: a movement delta plus the mouse's current button state, exactly as a real mouse would report one - one sample per call, not a batch. The X16's mouse is relative (PS/2-style), not absolute, so there's no "move to X,Y", only "move by this much from wherever the cursor already is". To click, send the button held (deltaX/deltaY 0 is fine) then send it released. Returns JSON: { "Success": boolean, "Error": string or null }.

deltaX.description: Horizontal movement since the last sample, in pixels. Positive is right. Defaults to 0.

deltaY.description: Vertical movement since the last sample, in pixels. Positive is down. Defaults to 0.

left.description: Whether the left button is currently held down.

right.description: Whether the right button is currently held down.

middle.description: Whether the middle button is currently held down.
